subject: Oceanography
title: Waves Approaching Shore
description: A 60-second lesson on Waves Approaching Shore.

hook.text: Waves always seem to arrive parallel to the beach—even if they started at an angle.

buildup.text: As waves enter shallow water, the bottom slows the lower part of the wave—this is called shoaling.

discovery.text: The part still in deeper water moves faster, bending the wave crest—this is wave refraction.

twist.text: Refraction focuses wave energy on headlands and spreads it in bays—shaping the coastline over time.

climax.text: Headlands erode while bays fill with sand—refraction slowly straightens jagged coastlines.

punchline.text: The seafloor bends waves—and waves reshape the coast.

quiz.question: What causes wave refraction?
options: The shallower part of a wave slows down first
